title: The rise and retreat of odd-toed ungulates
titleZh: 奇蹄目的兴衰
dek: From Eocene dominance to a small modern remnant, follow 56 million years of changing herbivore worlds.

steps.title: A rapid Eocene arrival
steps.text: Perissodactyls appear across northern continents and quickly diversify into horse-like, tapir-like, rhinoceros-like and wholly extinct forms.
steps.annotation: First appearances are fossil observations, not exact origination dates.

steps.title: Browsers in a greenhouse world
steps.text: Warm forests support palaeotheres, brontotheres and early rhinocerotoids across Eurasia and North America.

steps.title: Cooling changes the guild
steps.text: At the Eocene–Oligocene transition, climate, habitat and migration reorganize mammal communities; this is ecological turnover, not a simple competitive defeat.

steps.title: Specialists and survivors
steps.text: Horses, tapirs and rhinoceroses persist, but the modern order is only a narrow sample of its former ecological range.

title: Changing of the herbivore guild
titleZh: 大型有蹄动物生态位换班
dek: Compare ecological succession with ancestry—and see why resemblance does not imply descent.

steps.title: An odd-toed world
steps.text: Many Eocene large-herbivore guilds are rich in perissodactyl lineages that have no living equivalent.

steps.title: The rules change
steps.text: Cooling and increasingly seasonal habitats restructure vegetation and dispersal routes near 34 Ma.

steps.title: Overlap before replacement
steps.text: Miocene horses and rhinoceroses coexist with expanding deer, giraffids and bovids; turnover is prolonged and regionally variable.

title: Repeated returns to the water's edge
titleZh: 半水生哺乳动物的多次独立演化
dek: Metamynodon shows how body shape, eye position and sedimentary context can suggest—but not prove—behavior.

steps.title: A hippo-like rhinocerotoid
steps.text: Metamynodon combines short limbs, a broad trunk and high-set eyes in an animal unrelated to hippopotamuses.

steps.title: Deposits add context
steps.text: Frequent recovery from river sandstones strengthens the semi-aquatic interpretation, while still leaving behavior inferential.

steps.title: Convergence is not ancestry
steps.text: Later semi-aquatic artiodactyls occupy analogous guilds. Similar ecology evolved independently in separate branches.

title: Horses from forest browsers to open-country runners
titleZh: 马科从林地食叶者到草原奔跑者
dek: Horse evolution is a branching experiment, not a ladder marching toward one toe.

steps.title: Small forest equids
steps.text: Early horses retain multiple toes and low-crowned teeth in warm Eocene forests.

steps.title: Browsing persists
steps.text: Anchitherium carries a three-toed, low-crowned browsing strategy into the Miocene.

steps.title: Open habitats diversify the experiment
steps.text: Hipparionine horses spread widely and range from mixed feeders to specialized grazers; multiple lineages coexist.

title: Five mass extinctions
titleZh: 五次大灭绝
dek: Read extinction as changes in sampled ranges, ecological structure and Earth-system proxies.

steps.title: End-Ordovician
steps.text: Glaciation and sea-level change coincide with a major marine diversity loss.

steps.title: Late Devonian pulses
steps.text: Multiple crises affect reef and marine communities over an extended interval.

steps.title: The largest crisis
steps.text: The end-Permian event produces the deepest known Phanerozoic restructuring.

steps.title: End-Triassic
steps.text: Turnover across marine and terrestrial ecosystems precedes Jurassic dinosaur dominance.

steps.title: K–Pg
steps.text: The Chicxulub impact marks an abrupt global boundary and a selective survival event.

title: Seven evidence boundaries across the fin-to-limb transition
titleZh: 鳍—肢转型的七条证据边界
dek: Read tracks, articulated bodies, internal fin skeletons, digit-bearing limbs and mobility models as different evidence—not as a ladder of direct ancestors marching onto land.

steps.title: A mosaic, not a march
steps.text: A synthesis separates digit-bearing limbs, locomotor changes and full terrestriality. Its broad window organizes unlike evidence; it is not one event or an ancestor-to-descendant sequence.
steps.annotation: A transitional character combination can illuminate evolution without making its bearer the direct ancestor of another named fossil.

steps.title: Digits recorded without a body
steps.text: Eifelian Zachełmie surfaces preserve quadrupedal tracks and digit impressions. A trace constrains a trackmaker and gait, but cannot supply a named body taxon, complete anatomy or direct ancestor.
steps.annotation: The displayed interval is the current Eifelian stage window, not an error bar on one footprint.

steps.title: One body, aquatic and tetrapod-like characters
steps.text: Tiktaalik combines scales, fin rays and fish-like jaws with a mobile neck, modified ear region and robust ribs. Anatomy and setting make shallow-water hypotheses testable, not observed terrestrial behaviour.
steps.annotation: Intermediate morphology is not evidence that the specimen lies on a direct ancestral line.

steps.title: A mobile wrist still inside a fin
steps.text: Tiktaalik's pectoral fin has a robust internal scaffold and wrist-like joints that could transmit load, but fin rays remain and no free digits or track are preserved.
steps.annotation: Joint geometry supports a functional inference; it does not replay a witnessed gait.

steps.title: Digit-like rows beneath fin rays
steps.text: CT imaging of MHNM 06-2067 reveals branched carpals and distal rows interpreted as digits or putative digits. Lepidotrichia still make the appendage a fin.
steps.annotation: Digit homology and sister-group placement are analyses, not labels fixed forever by the specimen.

steps.title: Eight digits do not equal land walking
steps.text: Acanthostega's described forelimb has eight digits. Together with seven-digit Ichthyostega and six-digit Tulerpeton, it rejects a fixed primitive five-digit template without proving a terrestrial gait.
steps.annotation: Digit count, appendage function and habitat are separate claims.

steps.title: A mobility model, not a universal gait
steps.text: Three-dimensional joint reconstruction found that Ichthyostega lacked rotations needed for a typical lateral-sequence walk. It may represent restricted early mobility or a specialization unique to this animal.
steps.annotation: Feasible joint motion is a model constraint, not direct observation of behaviour and not a template for every Devonian tetrapod.

title: Mammals did not begin at K–Pg
titleZh: 哺乳动物并非在恐龙灭绝后才出现
dek: Mammals have a deep Mesozoic history; the boundary changes ecological opportunity, not their date of origin.

steps.title: A much older branch
steps.text: The synapsid lineage begins hundreds of millions of years before crown mammals.

steps.title: Mesozoic mammal diversity
steps.text: Small body size does not mean ecological uniformity: Mesozoic mammals include climbers, diggers, swimmers and gliders.

steps.title: Radiation after survival
steps.text: Surviving mammal lineages expand body size and guild diversity after 66 Ma.

title: From synapsids to mammals
titleZh: 从合弓纲到现代哺乳类
dek: Follow changes in jaws, ears, teeth and posture across one of the fossil record's classic transitions.

steps.title: The amniote split
steps.text: Synapsids and sauropsids diverge early in amniote history.

steps.title: Therapsid experiments
steps.text: Posture, feeding and skull architecture change across Permian and Triassic synapsids.

steps.title: A new jaw and middle ear
steps.text: The mammalian jaw joint and detached middle-ear bones emerge through a sequence of small-bodied forms.

title: How early land-plant evidence changes shape
titleZh: 早期陆生植物证据如何改变形态
dek: Move from a modelled crown divergence to dispersed cryptospores, spore-bearing fragments and anatomically informative Devonian bodies without collapsing them into one origin date.

steps.title: A modelled crown interval
steps.text: A fossil-calibrated relaxed clock places crown Embryophyta in a broad middle Cambrian–Early Ordovician interval, but this is a model result rather than a fossil occurrence.
steps.annotation: The Plantae node is navigation context; the claim concerns crown Embryophyta.

steps.title: Dispersed spores on emerged land
steps.text: A Dapingian assemblage in Argentina contains five cryptospore genera, but dispersed propagules do not reveal a complete parent plant or a crown-bryophyte identity.
steps.annotation: The source-reported numerical ages are retained; they are not silently replaced by the current ICS Dapingian boundaries.

steps.title: Spores linked to plant fragments
steps.text: Late Ordovician Oman fragments preserve dense spore masses and probable sporangial covering, strengthening the land-plant interpretation while leaving liverwort crown affinity tentative.
steps.annotation: The broad window translates a legacy Caradoc assignment for display; it is not a point date.

steps.title: A three-axis rooting system
steps.text: Three-dimensional fossil reconstruction shows how Asteroxylon combined leafy shoots, root-bearing axes and rooting axes through an extinct developmental pathway.
steps.annotation: A species-level exemplar cannot supply morphology for every lycophyte lineage.

steps.title: A liverwort body-fossil record
steps.text: Givetian Metzgeriothallus preserves thalloid gametophytes and an associated sporophyte capsule, adding body-plan information without turning one occurrence into a phylum origin date.
steps.annotation: Occurrence, morphology and crown divergence remain separate evidence objects.

title: Six boundaries in gymnosperm deep time
titleZh: 裸子植物深时研究的六条证据边界
dek: Read one fossil organ, several clock and biogeographic models, and a living-lineage topology without turning unlike evidence into one false origin timeline.

steps.title: One Jurassic wood specimen
steps.text: PB22285 preserves a Ginkgo-like combination of wood characters in 153–165 Ma strata, but an isolated organ cannot identify a complete plant or set the first appearance of Ginkgophyta.
steps.annotation: A specimen occurrence, a whole-plant association and a clade first appearance are three different claims.

steps.title: A crown age moves with calibration
steps.text: A plastome clock combining fossil and tectonic constraints places the living Cycadaceae crown much older than a Miocene-only story, while alternative schemes reveal wide model sensitivity.
steps.annotation: The event dates a modelled crown of living Cycadaceae, not the fossil first appearance of all cycads.

steps.title: Fossils change the map
steps.text: Adding fossil leaves to a species-level model expands inferred past cycad latitudes and multiplies inferred local extirpations, demonstrating that living distributions alone erase history.
steps.annotation: The wide interval summarizes a modelled transition; it is not one precisely dated global extinction pulse.

steps.title: A famous young-radiation model
steps.text: The 2011 estimate that most sampled living cycad species are no older than roughly 12 Ma remains historically important, but later fossil-integrated work prevents it from becoming the age of Cycadales.
steps.annotation: Living-species radiation, crown age, stem history and fossil first appearance must stay separate.

steps.title: A relative hemispheric pattern
steps.text: Southern Hemisphere conifer lineages in one living-species time tree have older median nodes than sampled northern lineages, but those medians are neither family origins nor fossil ranges.
steps.annotation: The comparison excludes Gnetales and does not validate the atlas's provisional Araucariaceae range.

steps.title: Topology is not a timeline
steps.text: A broad nuclear dataset recovers cycads plus Ginkgo and a Gnetales–Pinaceae relationship among living families, while gene-tree conflict and extinct lineages remain visible limits.
steps.annotation: This hypothesis does not replace the global navigation tree or supply chronological branch lengths.

title: Seven evidence boundaries in flowering-plant history
titleZh: 被子植物历史的七条证据边界
dek: Compare calibration-sensitive clocks, dated whole plants, regional phytolith assemblages and animal-diet isotopes without turning them into one false origin or dominance timeline.

steps.title: One dataset, three clock ranges
steps.text: A 2026 analysis integrates 25,685 fossil occurrences with molecular data, but its crown-angiosperm interval changes radically with calibration treatment; the narrow Late Jurassic result is the authors' preferred model, not a fossil flower.
steps.annotation: The atlas displays the preferred hard-bound result while exposing the much older alternatives beside it.

steps.title: Major lineages in an Early Cretaceous model
steps.text: A separate metacalibrated time tree places several major flowering-plant crown lineages near 135–130 Ma. Those estimates neither validate the atlas's legacy ranges nor record fossil first appearances.
steps.annotation: The navigation tree is an educational subset: monocots and eudicots do not exhaust Angiospermae, and Magnoliopsida is not an exact eudicot catalogue root.

steps.title: Many specimens, one extinct habit
steps.text: More than one thousand Montsechia specimens combine leafy axes, closed single-seeded fruits and depositional evidence for a submerged freshwater plant. They do not make the flowering-plant ancestor aquatic.
steps.annotation: A fossil habit, a phylogenetic placement and an ancestral ecological state are different claims.

steps.title: A dated eudicot whole plant
steps.text: Leefructus links diagnostic leaves and reproductive organs in a 125.8–122.6 Ma Yixian bed, supporting an early eudicot record while leaving Ranunculaceae affinity provisional.
steps.annotation: One locality cannot define the global origin, first appearance or diversity of eudicots.

steps.title: Roots and flowers in one monocot
steps.text: Cratolirion preserves roots, leaves, anatomy and reproductive organs together at about 115 Ma. Its crown-monocot placement does not turn it into a modern lily or the first monocot.
steps.annotation: Whole-plant preservation strengthens character association, not claims beyond the analysed specimen and placement.

steps.title: A regional grass-community proxy
steps.text: Fourteen Great Plains palaeosol assemblages record an 8–5.5 Ma increase in potentially C4 grass phytoliths. The 50–60% value applies within grasses, not to all vegetation.
steps.annotation: Regional assemblages and diagnostic limits prevent a synchronous global C4-grassland claim.

steps.title: Animal diets reveal C4 biomass
steps.text: Tooth-enamel carbon isotopes record widespread, regionally asynchronous C4 biomass expansion around 8–6 Ma. They do not identify the exact C4 plant lineages or directly measure open-grassland cover.
steps.annotation: Dietary isotope proxy, plant identity, vegetation cover and faunal adaptation must remain separate.

title: Three early-fish fossils, three different boundaries
titleZh: 三组早期鱼类化石，三条不同边界
dek: Move from an articulated stem gnathostome to lamprey and hagfish total-group fossils without turning specimen occurrences into crown origins or PBDB first appearances.

steps.title: An articulated jawed stem vertebrate
steps.text: IVPP V300001 and twenty referred Xiushanosteus specimens expose an approximately 436 Ma placoderm-grade body and mosaic skull roof. Abundance in one Lagerstätte does not make the animal a direct ancestor or a global first appearance.
steps.annotation: Articulation strengthens anatomical association; it does not convert a stem-grade taxon into a crown ancestor.

steps.title: A lamprey-like oral apparatus
steps.text: Holotype AM5750 preserves a large oral disc, fourteen circumoral teeth and a branchial basket at roughly 360 Ma. These structures diagnose total-group lamprey anatomy, not parasitism, migration or an ammocoete lifecycle.
steps.annotation: A body fossil can preserve adult-like structures while leaving lifecycle and crown-node timing unresolved.

steps.title: A stem hagfish is not crown Myxini
steps.text: FMNH PF15373 and PF8472 preserve a roughly 310–307 Ma cyclostome–hagfish mosaic, but different preservation and equivocal structures require a stem or putative total-group reading. The separate Myxini navigation node therefore does not inherit this age.
steps.annotation: Total-group occurrence and crown-group range are separate evidence objects.

title: Four specimens on the chondrichthyan stem
titleZh: 软骨鱼干群上的四组标本证据
dek: Compare isolated teeth, a disarticulated dermoskeleton, one armoured articulated body and a later compressed skeleton while keeping stem placement separate from crown sharks and global FAD claims.

steps.title: Direct teeth without a body
steps.text: Twenty-three Qianodus tooth whorls at roughly 439 Ma provide direct evidence of jawed-vertebrate dentition. No articulated jaw or body is known, and nearby scales and spines cannot be assigned by proximity alone.
steps.annotation: Earliest direct dental evidence in the study is narrower than the origin of jaws or crown Chondrichthyes.

steps.title: A shoulder assembled and remodelled
steps.text: Fanjingshania dermal elements from the same approximate age show a spine–plate complex that grew through multiple centres and cyclical tissue resorption. Disarticulation prevents a complete-body or associated-tooth claim.
steps.annotation: Co-occurrence of Qianodus and Fanjingshania is not evidence that they are the same animal.

steps.title: One articulated mosaic
steps.text: Shenacanthus combines minute scales and a chondrichthyan-like posterior branchial region with large thoracic armour at roughly 436 Ma. A single toothless holotype and method-sensitive placement block a crown-shark reading.
steps.annotation: A chondrichthyan total-group placement is not a diagnosis of the living shark crown.

steps.title: A later stem taxon remains unfamiliar
steps.text: At roughly 385 Ma, UMZC 2000.32 preserves jaws, gill arches, cartilage, scales and teeth in a surprising character mosaic. Compression, a missing tail and inferred feeding ecology remain visible limitations.
steps.annotation: The stable shark-like morphotype was assembled through a more disparate stem history than one specimen can summarize.

title: Seven evidence boundaries in ray-finned fish history
titleZh: 辐鳍鱼历史的七条证据边界
dek: Move from named Devonian and Triassic specimens to molecular models and living genomes without merging fossil occurrence, inferred event time, extant topology and nomenclatural coverage.

steps.title: A named Devonian anatomical mosaic
steps.text: CT scans connect particular Cheirolepis museum specimens to an imperforate propterygium and hyomandibular shaft plus peg-and-socket scales. The late Eifelian occurrence is not the global first ray-finned fish or a direct ancestor.
steps.annotation: Specimen anatomy, stage assignment and lineage origin are separate claims.

steps.title: A duplication interval from molecules
steps.text: Thirty duplicated-gene pairs place teleost 3R at 286.18–267.20 Ma in the study's models, before its crown-Teleostei interval. Neither interval is a fossil first appearance or an instantaneous observation.
steps.annotation: Duplication, rediploidization and later diversification are not one synchronous causal event.

steps.title: A fossil placement changes a calibration
steps.text: The 2017 analysis places Fukangichthys and other scanilepiforms on the polypterid stem, revising which fossils constrain the living crown. The result is topology-sensitive and differs from the published 2014 placement.
steps.annotation: A minimum calibration is younger than some previous calibrations; it is not the crown's birth time.

steps.title: Three stem teleosteomorphs at one quarry
steps.text: Named Rüdersdorf holotypes and referred specimens record distinct early teleosteomorph bodies near 244 Ma. Their stem placement and one-locality sample do not establish the crown-Teleostei FAD or a worldwide radiation.
steps.annotation: The current Anisian display envelope is broader than the source's approximate locality age.

steps.title: Living genomes support Holostei
steps.text: A spotted-gar genome, bowfin transcriptome and comparative synteny support gars plus bowfin as sister to teleosts. These present-day data do not directly date fossils or demonstrate unchanged anatomy.
steps.annotation: A genomic outgroup to teleost duplication is not a deterministic explanation for teleost richness.

steps.title: The tail complex crosses the gar–teleost split
steps.text: Gar and teleost developmental series share a hypural-diastema complex, while bowfin and other comparisons expose a mosaic. Descent with loss and latent parallelism remain alternative histories.
steps.annotation: Soft tissues and vasculature make the living complex richer than the component usually visible in fossils.

steps.title: Independent genomic markers resolve a deep split
steps.text: Gene trees and chromosome-adjacency markers support Elopomorpha plus Osteoglossomorpha as sister to Clupeocephala in the sampled living genomes. This is not a full species tree or a directly observed ancient fusion.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 routes 35,928 strictly accepted species names below Actinopterygii (usage ID 8VR36); that is naming coverage, not 35,928 mature dossiers, verified morphologies, fossil ranges, media records or expert reviews.

title: Five amphibian fossils, five boundaries
titleZh: 五组两栖类化石，五条证据边界
dek: Follow named specimens from a Permian stem batrachian to a provisional Oligocene crown-caecilian record without merging total groups, crowns, direct ancestry or global first appearances.

steps.title: A stem batrachian mosaic
steps.text: One Gerobatrachus holotype combines frog-like and salamander-like characters in the original tree, but it is not crown Batrachia or a direct ancestor.
steps.annotation: A proposed topology and a specimen occurrence are narrower than the origin of living amphibians.

steps.title: Hidden anatomy in a split nodule
steps.text: μCT reveals caudal vertebrae and a long trunk in the unique Triadobatrachus holotype, supporting stem Salientia rather than crown Anura or specialized jumping.
steps.annotation: Historical provenance and current numerical chart boundaries remain visibly separate.

steps.title: Many individuals, isolated elements
steps.text: At least 76 Funcusvermis individuals from a dated bonebed support Gymnophionomorpha while remaining outside crown Gymnophiona.
steps.annotation: A total-group occurrence cannot set the crown-group range.

steps.title: Articulated salamandroids below a dated flow
steps.text: PKUP V0601–V0606 support an Oxfordian salamandroid record; the zircon age comes from overlying rock and neoteny is inferred.
steps.annotation: Association strengthens anatomy while leaving age and developmental interpretation bounded.

steps.title: A provisional living-family assignment
steps.text: DGM 1462-R supports an Oligocene caecilian compared with living Typhlonectidae, but formal phylogenetic testing and an unambiguous family synapomorphy are absent.
steps.annotation: The crown display bound is deliberately low-confidence and revision-ready.

title: Living amphibian data: genome, experiment and tree
titleZh: 现生两栖动物数据：基因组、实验与系统树
dek: Compare one frog genome, receptor-knockout metamorphosis and a synthetic species timetree without treating extant datasets as fossils, ancestors or complete taxonomic coverage.

steps.title: One individual, one draft genome
steps.text: The Xenopus tropicalis draft assembly is a powerful extant reference with an accession and known sampling boundary, not a genome for all amphibians.
steps.annotation: Extant genomic comparison does not directly observe lineage origins.

steps.title: Metamorphosis differs by receptor and organ
steps.text: TRβ knockout delays tail regression while TRα knockout advances hindlimbs, making the experiment mechanistic but model- and tissue-specific.
steps.annotation: Experimental causation in one laboratory model is not a universal amphibian rule.

steps.title: Molecular and taxonomic placements coexist
steps.text: The 7,238-species posterior uses molecular data for 4,061 species and soft taxonomic inference for the rest; its times are model outputs.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 naming coverage, sequence sampling and mature evidence dossiers remain different inventories.

title: Seven evidence boundaries from synapsids to mammals
titleZh: 从合弓类到哺乳动物的七条证据边界
dek: Follow named specimens, CT datasets, character matrices and living experiments while keeping anatomy, topology, function, crown membership and time explicitly separate.

steps.title: One referred spine, not a finished sail
steps.text: ROM VP 83326 records striking neural-spine elongation in a referred early synapsid. Missing surrounding anatomy prevents the specimen from fixing whole-body proportions, function or a lineage-wide first appearance.
steps.annotation: A referred bone, a reconstructed body outline and a proposed sail function are three different evidence levels.

steps.title: A fragment enters a character matrix
steps.text: The partial snout IVPP V15424 was recovered beside the remaining sampled therapsids in one 71-character analysis. That topology is reproducible evidence, not direct ancestry or a precisely dated origin event.
steps.annotation: The paper itself warns that the Dashankou sequence lacks reliable radiometric dates.

steps.title: Two cynodont samples reject a simple ladder
steps.text: Riograndia has dentary–squamosal contact while the nine-specimen Brasilodon sample lacks it. The distribution supports iterative acquisition, and contact alone neither creates a crown mammal nor proves modern joint function.
steps.annotation: The 225.42 ± 0.37 Ma value is a maximum depositional age, not a direct fossil date.

steps.title: Crown membership is a tested topology
steps.text: CT anatomy and wear from MCZ7/95A–B and MCZ10/G95 reshaped a published matrix that placed Haramiyavia outside crown Mammalia. The placement belongs to that analysis, while the jaw surface only indirectly supports auditory anatomy.
steps.annotation: A matrix placement, a crown calibration and an anatomical observation are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Separate fossils show separate mosaics
steps.text: Dianoconodon and Feredocodon preserve different jaw–ear combinations across two formations and times. Their comparison supports a load shift, but it is not a continuous transformation series or an ancestor–descendant pair.
steps.annotation: Preserved contacts support, but do not directly measure, biting and hearing performance.

steps.title: Detached bones can retain a cartilage link
steps.text: IVPP V16051 preserves ectotympanic and malleus elements separated from direct dentary contact yet connected by ossified Meckel's cartilage. One articulated skeleton documents a mosaic, not a universal evolutionary stage.
steps.annotation: Anatomical connection is observed; stabilization and auditory effects remain functional inference.

steps.title: Living development tests a mechanism, not ancestry
steps.text: Mouse genetics and opossum inhibition experiments show that disrupting clast-cell activity can retain a jaw–ear cartilage connection. They illuminate a possible mechanism without replaying a particular fossil or proving its ancient cause.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 assigns zero accepted species directly to mammal-origins because living Mammalia route to order-specific or other-mammals packages and Synapsida lacks a reliable materialized species root. Zero is a routing boundary, not evidence of no living synapsids, no nomenclatural coverage or complete dossier maturity.

title: Three reptile radiations, nine evidence dossiers
titleZh: 三次爬行动物辐射与九个证据档案
dek: Compare named ichthyosaur, plesiosaur and pterosaur evidence without turning independent radiations, fossil occurrences, functional models or database naming coverage into one ancestor ladder.

steps.title: A short-snouted ichthyosauromorph holotype
steps.text: AGM I-1 preserves a small short-snouted body with large flippers and dense limb and rib bone. Amphibious habits and suction feeding are functional interpretations, not recorded behaviour or proof of direct ancestry.
steps.annotation: The corrigendum is part of the evidence record; it changed character descriptions and tree statistics while retaining the reported topology.

steps.title: Pregnancy is stronger evidence than reconstructed birth history
steps.text: Maternal Chaohusaurus specimen AGM I-1 contains two embryos and an adjacent neonate. Their association supports pregnancy, whereas head-first delivery and a terrestrial origin of viviparity remain comparative inferences.
steps.annotation: A specimen-level reproductive record does not define the ancestral state of all marine reptiles.

steps.title: Skin chemistry from one Jurassic ichthyosaur
steps.text: MH 432 preserves skin layers, a blubber-like subcutaneous layer and eumelanin-bearing structures. Countershading and thermoregulation are interpretations from distribution and living comparisons, not directly measured physiology.
steps.annotation: One exceptional specimen does not establish a universal tissue condition for Ichthyosauria.

steps.title: A Rhaetian plesiosaur skeleton and histology
steps.text: LWL-MFN P 64047 supplies articulated anatomy and vascularized long-bone tissue from the Rhaetian. Basal pliosaurid placement and physiological implications remain dependent on phylogenetic and histological interpretation.
steps.annotation: A named Triassic skeleton is not automatically the global first occurrence or a direct ancestor of later plesiosaurs.

steps.title: A fetus documents plesiosaur viviparity
steps.text: Adult Polycotylus LACM 129639 contains one large articulated fetus identified as the same taxon. Pregnancy and viviparity are specimen evidence; parental care, sociality and K-selection are broader analogical hypotheses.
steps.annotation: Preserved reproductive anatomy and inferred life-history strategy have different evidentiary strength.

steps.title: Four flippers tested in a water channel
steps.text: A physical model measured thrust and efficiency at prescribed fore- and hind-flipper phase offsets. Vortex interaction supports mechanical plausibility, not a filmed extinct gait or one stroke shared by every plesiosaur.
steps.annotation: Model inputs, measured outputs and palaeobiological extrapolation remain separate.

steps.title: Branched structures and melanosomes on one skull
steps.text: MCT.R.1884 preserves monofilaments, branched feather-like structures and melanosomes around a Tupandactylus skull and crest. The evidence does not directly recover exact colours or a universal pterosaur covering.
steps.annotation: Preserved structures, colour-function hypotheses and reconstructed ancestral states are different claim types.

steps.title: Hundreds of eggs, sixteen with embryos
steps.text: A Hamipterus block exposes 215 eggs and may contain about 300; sixteen eggs in the wider assemblage preserve embryonic remains across multiple levels. Nesting, transport and hatchling behaviour remain interpretations.
steps.annotation: Egg and embryo counts do not by themselves demonstrate parental care or post-hatching flight capacity.

steps.title: Quadrupedal launch is a feasibility model
steps.text: Scaling, bone mechanics and aerodynamic calculations make powered flight and forelimb-assisted launch feasible for sampled giant-pterosaur reconstructions. The model is not direct observation of an extinct takeoff.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 contributes zero accepted species through these fossil-root routes; naming coverage and dossier maturity are independent, and the three radiations remain separate.

title: Eight whale-transition dossiers without an ancestor ladder
titleZh: 不构成祖先阶梯的八个鲸类转型档案
dek: Follow named fossils, separate specimen assemblages and living molecular datasets while keeping anatomy, ecology, topology, model time and COL26.8 naming coverage distinct.

steps.title: Several samples support one bounded inference
steps.text: RR 207 and RR 208 skulls, separate dense limb bones and tooth isotopes support aquatic wading and raoellid affinity. They are not one skeleton, crown whales or proof that Indohyus directly became a whale.
steps.annotation: Specimens, ecological interpretation and matrix placement remain separate evidence levels.

steps.title: A reconstruction can combine individuals
steps.text: Pakicetus skull H-GSP 96231 and separately catalogued postcranial bones from Locality 62 support a terrestrial body plan. The published outline is a composite, not one articulated animal or a direct ancestor.
steps.annotation: The 2001 morphology tree and the independent 1999 retroposon tree answer different sampled questions.

steps.title: One holotype, a locomotor mosaic
steps.text: H-GSP 18507 preserves an amphibious combination of vertebral and limb anatomy. Otter-like swimming and sea-lion-like terrestrial motion are functional models, not observed strokes or gait.
steps.annotation: A named specimen can constrain mechanical possibility without recording behaviour.

steps.title: A dated occurrence is firmer than a route
steps.text: MUSM 3580 fixes a roughly 42.6 Ma protocetid occurrence in Peru and preserves weight-bearing anatomy. Its walking, swimming and westward Atlantic dispersal narratives are tested interpretations, not a filmed journey.
steps.annotation: The paper explicitly leaves an eastward route and the presence of a tail fluke unresolved.

steps.title: A tiny foot is not a walking foot
steps.text: Basilosaurus retains a miniature jointed pelvic limb and foot, and UM 93231 preserves measurable femoral microstructure. Neither establishes terrestrial locomotion; copulatory use remains inferred.
steps.annotation: Preserved anatomy, measured tissue and proposed function are three distinct claims.

steps.title: Tail propulsion without a preserved fluke
steps.text: CGM 60584 records unfused sacrals, no weight-bearing sacroiliac joint, posterior vertebral elongation and reduced limbs. Greater tail propulsion is inferred, while a fluke is doubtful and not preserved.
steps.annotation: The source itself discloses conflicting age indicators around the Bartonian–Priabonian boundary.

steps.title: Living genomes test a branch, not an age
steps.text: Independent retroposon insertions support Hippopotamidae as the living sister group of Cetacea. The sampled topology does not identify a direct ancestor, date the split or place every fossil relative.
steps.annotation: Molecular topology and fossil character placement remain independently inspectable.

steps.title: A 2009 tree is not a 2026 catalogue
steps.text: The 42,335-character supermatrix sampled 87 of 89 cetacean species recognized in 2009. Its tree and clock estimates are model results, whereas COL26.8 is the pinned authority for current accepted-name routing.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 routes 503 strictly accepted species through the package's exact Artiodactyla and Cetacea usage roots; that is naming coverage, not 503 molecular trees, fossil dossiers or reviewed ranges.

title: Eight evidence mosaics in turtle and lepidosaur origins
titleZh: 龟类与鳞龙起源的八组证据镶嵌
dek: Move from named bones and CT volumes to competing matrices and clock calibrations without turning separate fossils into an ancestor ladder.

steps.title: A rib section tests a shell model
steps.text: NHM PV R 4949 shows successive bone deposition in a broadened Eunotosaurus rib, while other specimens preserve shoulder anatomy. The tissue is observed; turtle-stem placement, homology and function are tested interpretations.
steps.annotation: Separate preserved tissue from a character-homology model and from direct ancestry.

steps.title: Paired gastralia without a finished plastron
steps.text: The Vellberg Pappochelys sample combines broad ribs and robust paired gastralia but lacks a fused plastron and complete carapace. Serial fusion is a homology hypothesis, not a frame in a literal ancestor sequence.
steps.annotation: A multi-specimen reconstruction is not one individual transforming into a later taxon.

steps.title: A complete plastron and incomplete dorsal shell
steps.text: Three Odontochelys specimens preserve a developed plastron with expanded ribs and neural plates but no complete carapace. A plastron-first sequence and marginal-marine life remain interpretations, not anatomy seen changing through time.
steps.annotation: Shell elements, environmental setting and a proposed evolutionary order are distinct claim layers.

steps.title: One fossil sets a minimum, not an origin date
steps.text: Caribemys holotype MNHNCu P-3209 anchors a 155.6 Ma hard minimum for crown Testudines in one best-practice analysis. Its much older posterior estimate comes from a relaxed clock, topology and priors.
steps.annotation: A fossil minimum, a maximum prior and a posterior node age are three different quantities.

steps.title: A three-dimensional skull enters several trees
steps.text: Micro-CT reveals the cranial mosaic of Taytalura holotype PVSJ 698. Multiple analyses place it on the lepidosauromorph stem, but a single skull does not supply whole-body anatomy, direct ancestry or a global range.
steps.annotation: The scan volume is specimen evidence; the tree position is an analytical output.

steps.title: One skeleton joins morphology and molecules
steps.text: CT anatomy of Megachirella PZO 628 was combined with fossil morphology and living molecular partitions. The analysis recovers a stem squamate and estimates deep divergences, but neither output is a directly observed crown FAD.
steps.annotation: Fossil anatomy, molecular constraint and clock time remain separately labelled.

steps.title: A near-complete skeleton still gives a mosaic
steps.text: Synchrotron scans of Bellairsia NMS G.2022.1.1 reveal crown-like and retained states in one Jurassic skeleton. Stem placement and proposed cranial motion depend on matrices and functional interpretation.
steps.annotation: Completeness improves observation but does not remove topology or function uncertainty.

steps.title: The same block supports competing placements
steps.text: Teams disagree over bones, referrals and character scores for Cryptovaranoides NHMUK PV R36822, producing crown-squamate and non-squamate trees. The atlas therefore keeps the topology contested instead of inventing a secure Triassic crown FAD.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 assigns 12,622 accepted living species to this package as a nomenclatural routing snapshot; it neither resolves fossil topology nor measures dossier, translation, media or review maturity.

title: Two archosaur branches, eleven evidence dossiers
titleZh: 两条主龙支系与十一个证据档案
dek: Keep named specimens, feather chemistry, wind-tunnel measurements, phylogenetic topology, molecular clocks and COL26.8 living-name coverage separate while comparing crocodile-line and bird-line evidence.

steps.title: A suchian can resemble a theropod
steps.text: AMNH FR 30587 records an edentulous, gracile suchian. Its ornithomimid-like proportions are a convergence diagnosis, not evidence that the two branches share an immediate ancestor or identical ecology.
steps.annotation: Effigia is a pseudosuchian outside Crocodylomorpha, so it remains event evidence rather than a false child of the crocodile navigation node.

steps.title: A partial holotype, a bounded predator inference
steps.text: NCSM 21558 documents a large Carnian crocodylomorph. Size and predator tier come from proxies and assemblage context, not preserved feeding behaviour.
steps.annotation: Incomplete and immature anatomy cannot establish a direct ancestor or universal global first occurrence.

steps.title: Skull consolidation appears as a mosaic
steps.text: IVPP V14010 combines a consolidated, crocodylian-like skull with a gracile terrestrial postcranium. It is one anatomical mosaic rather than a compulsory stage in a ladder.
steps.annotation: Skull mechanics and cursoriality are functional interpretations; topology is character-matrix evidence.

steps.title: Living gharials meet fossils in a tip-dated model
steps.text: A combined morphology, molecular and age model groups Gavialis with Tomistoma while moving sampled thoracosaurs outside the crown. Other analyses differ.
steps.annotation: A preferred topology is not an observed genealogy; priors, weights and sampled characters remain visible boundaries.

steps.title: Archaeopteryx preserves an anatomical mosaic
steps.text: WDC CSG 100 exposes theropod-like pedal and palate features alongside avialan anatomy. The mosaic supports affinity without turning one specimen into the unique first bird.
steps.annotation: Joint posture, perching and exact placement are interpretations rather than direct observations.

steps.title: Microscopy informs a colour reconstruction
steps.text: Melanosomes in BMNHC PH828 support a statistical map of plumage regions. Preservation, reference samples and a tail borrowed from another specimen constrain the image.
steps.annotation: Anchiornis remains a non-avian paravian event here, not a false child of Aves or a directly observed ancestral colour state.

steps.title: Four feathered surfaces are preserved
steps.text: IVPP V13352 preserves long pennaceous feathers on forelimbs, hindlimbs and tail. The fossil records surfaces, not a flight trajectory.
steps.annotation: Microraptor is treated as a non-avian paravian dossier, not a direct bird ancestor.

steps.title: A wind tunnel tests feasibility
steps.text: Measured forces on a scaled model support stable high-drag gliding across tested configurations. That experiment is functional evidence, not footage of extinct behaviour.
steps.annotation: Geometry, scaling, reconstructed posture and fossil distortion bound every aerodynamic conclusion.

steps.title: One skull, two nearby crown placements
steps.text: CT anatomy anchors NHMM 2013 008 near Galloanserae, but parsimony and tip-dated Bayesian analyses place it on different branches.
steps.annotation: A tightly dated occurrence is not automatically the globally oldest modern bird, and crown membership remains analysis-dependent.

steps.title: Whole genomes still retain difficult branches
steps.text: Forty-eight representatives across neoavian orders recover major groupings and expose gene-tree conflict. This is sampled extant topology, not a complete species tree.
steps.annotation: Incomplete lineage sorting, convergence, sampling and method choice remain explicit.

steps.title: A calibrated time tree is a model
steps.text: Clock-like exons, broader RAG sampling and fossils infer a Cretaceous root and boundary-era radiation. The dates follow calibrations, topology and priors.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 routes 11,071 accepted living species into this package. That is a nomenclatural coverage boundary, not fossil completeness, direct ancestry or agreement on a single crown-bird date.

title: Twelve primate dossiers without an ancestor ladder
titleZh: 不构成祖先阶梯的十二个灵长类档案
dek: Move from a calibration-sensitive crown model through named fossils and ancient genomes while keeping specimens, functions, topology, model time and COL26.8 naming coverage distinct.

steps.title: A crown interval is not a fossil
steps.text: The selected clock model places crown Primates at 79.2–70.0 Ma, while another calibration strategy spans 71.4–63.9 Ma. Neither interval is a fossil occurrence.
steps.annotation: Clock and fossil priors materially change deep-node ages.

steps.title: An ankle attribution is bounded
steps.text: UCMP 197509, UCMP 197517 and related isolated tarsals preserve arboreal morphology. Their attribution to Purgatorius does not make them crown primates or a global first appearance.
steps.annotation: Isolated tarsals, dental attribution and functional inference are three steps.

steps.title: Ten teeth do not settle a crown
steps.text: THR 141 and a small isolated-tooth hypodigm define Altiatlasius, but tooth positions, membership and euprimate placement remain disputed.
steps.annotation: The existence of specimens is firmer than their topology.

steps.title: A correlated sequence is not one migration
steps.text: Asian, European and North American Teilhardina samples align to the PETM in a rapid appearance sequence, without recording one travelling lineage.
steps.annotation: Dental taxonomy and isotope correlation bound the dispersal inference.

steps.title: A digit can constrain function
steps.text: AMNH 143612/143640 preserves a ray-identified foot; digit-two phalanx AMNH 143612-03 supports a grooming-claw comparison, not crown-anthropoid ancestry.
steps.annotation: Preserved phalanx geometry is distinct from behaviour and topology.

steps.title: One skeleton, two slabs and a disclosure
steps.text: PMO 214.214 and WDC-MG-210 are opposite slabs of one Darwinius skeleton. Fabricated preparation on part of the counterplate is disclosed and crown placement remains contested.
steps.annotation: Exceptional completeness does not remove preparation and topology limits.

steps.title: Postcrania test a stem placement
steps.text: Eosimias-attributed tali and calcanei preserve a character mosaic used to test stem-anthropoid affinity, but they are isolated from diagnostic teeth.
steps.annotation: Matrix placement is not direct skeletal association or crown membership.

steps.title: A stem catarrhine is not the split itself
steps.text: SGS-UM 2009-002 preserves catarrhine anatomy and is recovered on the stem in one matrix. Its biochronological age does not directly date the ape–Old World monkey split.
steps.annotation: Specimen anatomy, matrix topology and crown divergence time stay separate.

steps.title: Separate bones support a locomotor model
steps.text: MUZM 60 and MUZM 80 come from different Moroto localities. Shoulder and femoral anatomy constrain a mixed arboreal model, not one skeleton or observed behaviour.
steps.annotation: The overlying basalt supplies a minimum-age constraint, not a direct specimen date.

steps.title: One skull expands observed variation
steps.text: D4500 and D2600 form Dmanisi Skull 5 at about 1.8 Ma. It documents one individual and a five-cranium sample, not a final decision that all early Homo names are one lineage.
steps.annotation: Taxonomic compression is an interpretation of variation, not part of the skull.

steps.title: A fragment can carry a population model
steps.text: Vindija 33.19 yielded a high-coverage Neanderthal genome and a >45.5 ka direct result. The roughly 52 ka age and population histories are branch-shortening and demographic models.
steps.annotation: Direct radiocarbon bounds and genomic time estimates are not interchangeable.

steps.title: A dated genome bounds contact indirectly
steps.text: Ust’-Ishim 1 is directly dated to 46,880–43,210 cal BP and deposited as PRJEB6622. Neanderthal segment length models earlier admixture but not its exact place or number of episodes.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 routes 530 accepted species names to this package; that is naming coverage, not 530 fossil or genome dossiers.

title: Eleven dossiers across carnivoran origins, form and function
titleZh: 横跨食肉类起源、形态与功能的十一个证据档案
dek: Follow named teeth, skulls, skeletons, sequence matrices and digital experiments without converting separate branches into an ancestor ladder.

steps.title: Hundreds of elements replace a two-tooth sketch
steps.text: IRSNB M2095–M2099 document reconstructed permanent dentition, while astragali IRSNB M2107–M2108 and calcaneum IRSNB M2109 document the tarsus.
steps.annotation: Dormaalocyon is recovered as a basal carnivoraform in the published character matrix; it is not demonstrated to be crown Carnivora, a direct ancestor or the global first carnivoramorphan.

steps.title: Traditional “miacoids” do not make two neat stems
steps.text: The matrix samples 99 cranial and dental characters across 40 terminals and excludes traditional “Miacidae” and Viverravidae from crown Carnivora in the preferred trees.
steps.annotation: This result rejects a convenient feliform–caniform ancestor ladder but remains a sampled morphology topology whose nodes can change with scoring, taxon sampling and analytical assumptions.

steps.title: A cranium tests the base of Caniformia
steps.text: Holotype UCMP 85202 supplies the cranium and dentition; associated paratypes SDSNH 107446 and SDSNH 107447 add postcranial anatomy.
steps.annotation: Basal-caniform placement is an analytical result and familial assignment remains indeterminate; dietary discriminant scores are comparative-model outputs, not stomach contents or observed hunting.

steps.title: Living sequences separate two crown branches
steps.text: The concatenated matrix contains 6,243 base pairs from TR-i-I, TBG, IRBP, ND2, CYTB and 12S rRNA for 76 sampled species.
steps.annotation: This is a 2005 sequence topology for sampled living taxa; it neither observes fossil anatomy nor fixes fossil first appearances, divergence dates or COL26.8 accepted names.

steps.title: Two Texas “Miacis” species are rescored
steps.text: The holotype cranium of Gustafsonia cognita, TMM 40209-200, was CT-reconstructed; Angelarctocyon australis is represented by TMM 41850-1 and referred jaw material.
steps.annotation: The new genera and basal-amphicyonid positions follow revised scoring and sampled trees; they do not locate an exact geographic origin for beardogs or establish direct ancestry.

steps.title: A digital mandible tests loading scenarios
steps.text: Holotype B-4071 is a complete young-adult skull; the 2026 analysis compares intrinsic canine, p4 and m1 bites and extrinsic pull-back and head-shaking loads, with meshes and scripts deposited on Zenodo.
steps.annotation: Stress fields, relative bite forces and behavioural scenarios depend on segmentation, material properties, muscle reconstruction, constraints and normalization; they are experiments on models, not observed feeding.

steps.title: Three dental records test panda affinity
steps.text: Holotype MNCN-CSIC NV-2-42 is a left P4; NV-2-40 is a right M1, and IPS 46473 is a partial mandible with c1–m2 and associated P4.
steps.annotation: Ailuropodine placement and herbivorous tendency derive from a character matrix and dental comparison; neither demonstrates identical giant-panda ecology nor a direct ancestor or secure centre of origin.

steps.title: A Tibetan skull enters a combined tree
steps.text: Holotype IVPP V18788.1 is an adult partial cranium; IVPP V18788.2 is a ramus fragment and IVPP V18788.3 a partial premaxilla. The locality sample spans 5.95–4.10 Ma in the original magnetostratigraphic framework.
steps.annotation: The original Panthera assignment, snow-leopard affinity and Asian biogeographic scenario are analytical conclusions that later work may revise; the sample is not a universal pantherine FAD.

steps.title: An inner ear predicts rather than preserves a hunt
steps.text: The 36-specimen sample includes Field Museum Hesperocyon gregarius and Aelurodon skulls, segmented as left bony labyrinths and compared by PCA, CVA and MANOVA.
steps.annotation: The reported 82.05% classification and pounce assignment are proxy-model results conditioned on living categories, scaling and phylogeny; they do not preserve an actual hunt or social behaviour.

steps.title: A lake skeleton mixes land and water traits
steps.text: Holotype NUFV 405 preserves roughly 65% of one skeleton, including skull, dentition, vertebrae and substantial fore- and hind limbs from an early Miocene lake deposit.
steps.annotation: Semi-aquatic locomotion, pinnipedimorph position and an Arctic freshwater transition are morphology, topology and palaeoenvironmental interpretations; Puijila is not demonstrated as a direct pinniped ancestor.

steps.title: A stem-pinniped skeleton tests swimming mechanics
steps.text: LACM 4321 preserves a skull and much of the postcranial skeleton, allowing measured limb proportions and joint morphology to be compared with living pinnipeds and terrestrial carnivorans.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 routes 310 accepted living species names through Carnivora. This is nomenclatural coverage, not eleven ancestor stages, 310 mature dossiers, a fossil FAD, or agreement among topology and clock models.

title: Other mammals: twelve evidence dossiers, no ancestor ladder
titleZh: 其他哺乳类：十二个证据档案而非祖先阶梯
dek: Compare named fossils, a living genome, morphology matrices, bone-density measurements and molecular trees while keeping specimen facts, function, topology, clocks and COL26.8 name routing separate.

steps.title: Steropodon jaw and monotreme dental evidence
steps.text: AM F66763 preserves a right dentary fragment and three molars whose morphology was compared with monotreme and tribosphenic conditions.
steps.annotation: Dental homology and affinity are interpretations; one jaw cannot establish a direct ancestor, a complete body plan or an immutable global first occurrence.

steps.title: Platypus draft genome and comparative mosaic
steps.text: Approximately 26.9 million reads produced a 1.84-gigabase draft at about sixfold coverage, with 437 megabases ordered on 20 chromosomes and 18,527 predicted protein-coding genes.
steps.annotation: Assembly gaps, one-individual sampling, annotation and comparative models prevent direct reconstruction of an ancestral genome or single-gene explanations for organismal traits.

steps.title: Eomaia skeleton, topology and locomotor inference
steps.text: CAGS 01-IG-1a,b documents the skull, dentition and much of the postcranium; the original matrix and limb comparisons supported a basal eutherian and scansorial interpretation.
steps.annotation: Later combined matrices can move Eomaia outside Theria; topology and scansoriality are analytical outputs, not a directly observed ancestor or behaviour.

steps.title: Juramaia specimen and conditional Jurassic signal
steps.text: BMNH PM1343B preserves skull, dentition and postcranium; the original study attributed it to approximately 160-million-year-old strata and recovered a basal eutherian position.
steps.annotation: Commercial collection provenance, stratigraphic attribution and matrices condition the result; unconstrained tip dating yields a younger morphological age signal rather than directly redating the rock.

steps.title: Ambolestes and a revised therian boundary
steps.text: STM33-5 preserves ectotympanic, malleus and hyoid anatomy; the published matrix recovers Ambolestes and Sinodelphys in Eutheria.
steps.annotation: Reassignment and the resulting metatherian ghost lineage depend on sampled characters and taxa; the analysis does not observe the placental–marsupial split.

steps.title: Placental phenomic matrix and K–Pg model
steps.text: The study scored 4,541 phenomic characters for 86 living and fossil species, supported by more than 12,000 annotated images, and combined them with 27 nuclear genes.
steps.annotation: The post-K–Pg chronology and reconstructed phenotype depend on parsimony, fossil ages, ghost lineages and ancestral-state optimization; no ancestor was directly observed.

steps.title: Placental four-clade molecular topology
steps.text: The 16,397-base-pair matrix combines 19 nuclear and 3 mitochondrial genes; Bayesian and maximum-likelihood analyses recover four major placental clades.
steps.annotation: The Afrotheria root, dates and Gondwanan scenario are model-conditioned, later studies test alternatives, and sampled taxa from other packages remain cross-boundary inputs.

steps.title: Eritherium skull and stem-proboscidean placement
steps.text: Holotype MNHN PM69 preserves a rostrum and maxillary dentition; fourteen additional specimens extend the sampled upper and lower teeth and skull anatomy.
steps.annotation: Stem placement and estimated 3–8 kilogram body mass derive from a character matrix and dental allometry, not observed ancestry or body mass.

steps.title: Thalassocnus bone-density series
steps.text: CT slices and thin sections show increasing compactness across ribs and limb bones, including named T. littoralis specimens MNHN.F.SAS 2 and MNHN.F.SAS 53.
steps.annotation: Aquatic adaptation, hydrostatic control and marine grazing are functional interpretations; species succession is not a directly observed ancestor chain.

steps.title: Mimolagus teeth, tarsals and body-size model
steps.text: Holotype right M3 IVPP V20115 and referred teeth, astragalus, calcanei and cuboid establish the anatomical sample and locality.
steps.annotation: A 4.5-kilogram estimate, cursoriality and tapiroid-like niche are regression and ecomorphology inferences; the taxon is not a direct lagomorph ancestor.

steps.title: Onychonycteris flight and echolocation proxies
steps.text: ROM 55351A preserves elongated wings and a relatively small cochlea; limb proportions and cochlear size were compared with living and fossil bats.
steps.annotation: Powered flight and absence of specialized laryngeal echolocation are functional inferences, not observed behaviour, and one specimen is not a direct ancestor.

steps.title: Seven-gene bat topology and echolocation scenarios
steps.text: Four nuclear and three mitochondrial genes contributed 8,230 aligned base pairs; analyses group sampled rhinolophoids with megabats rather than other microbats.
steps.annotation: Multiple origins or losses of laryngeal echolocation are alternative historical reconstructions; the topology does not directly observe the first flight or sonar event. COL26.8 routes 5,099 accepted living species to other-mammals after excluding Cetartiodactyla, Perissodactyla, Primates and Carnivora; that nomenclatural snapshot is not 5,099 dossiers and does not resolve fossil topology.

title: Twelve dinosaur dossiers without an ancestor ladder
titleZh: 不构成祖先阶梯的十二个恐龙档案
dek: Compare named specimens, morphology matrices, histology, taphonomy and functional models while preserving every observation–interpretation boundary and handing Avialae/flight evidence to the crocodylomorphs-birds package.

steps.title: One matrix does not settle the root
steps.text: Baron et al. recovered Ornithoscelida from 457 characters; Langer et al. recovered the traditional split after rescoring and added taxa. Both are topology tests.
steps.annotation: The 233–228 Ma atlas interval is a display context for early dinosaur fossils, not an age inferred by either morphology matrix.

steps.title: Teeth bound an ancestral-diet model
steps.text: ULBRA-PVT280 preserves recurved serrated teeth. Faunivory near the sauropodomorph root is an ancestral-state model, not a direct ancestor.
steps.annotation: Formation correlation bounds the age; the dietary transition is a mapped hypothesis across sampled taxa, not a linear sequence observed in one lineage.

steps.title: A partial skeleton tests an early branch
steps.text: SAM-PK-K8025 is a bounded partial skeleton. Matrix placement and formation age do not establish a global ornithischian first appearance.
steps.annotation: The broad display interval follows formation-level correlation and must not be read as a direct specimen date or a global ornithischian FAD.

steps.title: One species changes stance while growing
steps.text: Mussaurus digital models combine several growth stages. The bipedal-to-quadrupedal shift is ontogenetic and modelled, not an evolutionary ladder.
steps.annotation: The fossils constrain anatomy; centre of mass and stance are sensitivity-tested reconstructions and cannot be generalized to every sauropodomorph.

steps.title: Gigantism precedes columnar limbs
steps.text: BP/1/7120 supports an adult giant with flexed limbs. Twelve tonnes and habitual quadrupedality are comparative estimates from a partial skeleton.
steps.annotation: The specimen is incomplete and the earliest-Jurassic interval is formation-bounded; it is not a universal threshold or ancestor for sauropod gigantism.

steps.title: Armour is anatomy; placement is analysis
steps.text: NHMUK R1111 preserves associated osteoderms. Lost armour, inferred keratin and stem-ankylosaur placement remain separate from observation.
steps.annotation: Missing armour and preparation history prevent a complete in-place map; placement is one analysis rather than an uncontested thyreophoran topology.

steps.title: A complete skeleton tests a character mosaic
steps.text: IVPP V14530 preserves a nearly complete early ceratopsian skeleton. Its topology is a matrix result, not a direct ancestor.
steps.annotation: The atlas interval is formation-level; topology and character polarity depend on outgroups, coding and the sampled matrix.

steps.title: Skin and damage constrain taphonomy
steps.text: NDGS 2000 preserves skin and feeding traces. Scavenging-assisted desiccation is a pathway inferred for this carcass, not a universal rule.
steps.annotation: The evidence concerns one specimen and one depositional history; skin presence does not establish original colour, physiology or preservation frequency.

steps.title: Filaments do not require a flight story
steps.text: Three Yutyrannus skeletons preserve filamentous integument. Function, complete coverage and Avialae flight are separate questions.
steps.annotation: Non-avian integument stays here; Avialae, flight models and living-bird COL26.8 names remain owned by crocodylomorphs-birds.

steps.title: A pose supports but cannot observe brooding
steps.text: IGM 100/979 lies over a clutch in a bird-like posture. Brooding is well supported but remains behaviour inferred from association.
steps.annotation: The original paper explicitly retains alternative explanations and limits testing of parental-system hypotheses in the fossil record.

steps.title: Growth marks feed a fitted curve
steps.text: Tyrannosaurid growth marks are observations; reconstructed ages, masses and logistic growth rates are model outputs.
steps.annotation: The 83–66 Ma atlas window spans sampled tyrannosaurids, not one population; the fitted curve is not a universal dinosaur growth schedule.

steps.title: Traces and mechanics answer different questions
steps.text: MOR 799 traces and bone-bearing coprolite support osteophagy, while force and pressure derive from a seven-skull biomechanical model.
steps.annotation: The models test capability rather than observe a feeding event; MOR 799 and the coprolite do not identify every individual or every feeding context.

title: Fourteen sponge and cnidarian dossiers without a first-animal ladder
titleZh: 不构成“第一动物”阶梯的十四个海绵与刺胞动物档案
dek: Move from contested Cryogenian molecules through named Ediacaran and Cambrian fossils to living genomes, coral clocks and ecological proxies while keeping compounds, specimens, topology, model time and COL26.8 names distinct.

steps.title: A molecule is not a unique animal
steps.text: The Oman steranes are real measurements, but Rhizaria make relevant precursors. The package records a contested source attribution rather than a Cryogenian sponge fossil.
steps.annotation: Chemical occurrence and taxonomic diagnosis stay separate.

steps.title: One cellular fossil stays one sample
steps.text: Eocyathispongia preserves striking cellular organization, but the dossier does not turn funnel-like openings into a secure crown-sponge diagnosis.
steps.annotation: Imaged anatomy is firmer than affinity.

steps.title: An organic lattice tests a crown hypothesis
steps.text: Helicolocellus combines repeated body-wall grids with a morphology-matrix placement. Architecture is observed; hexactinellid affinity is inferred.
steps.annotation: Organic skeleton and siliceous spicule are not synonyms.

steps.title: Diagnostic criteria move the boundary
steps.text: The Soltanieh spicules survive a candidate-by-candidate reassessment, while older claims fail different taphonomic or diagnostic tests.
steps.annotation: A review boundary is revisable, not eternal.

steps.title: A toolkit is not a body plan
steps.text: Amphimedon retains extensive animal gene machinery. Comparative presence does not mean a sponge expresses bilaterian organs or mirrors the first animal.
steps.annotation: Genome content and phenotype remain distinct evidence.

steps.title: The root depends on the model
steps.text: Porifera-sister and Ctenophora-sister each have genome-scale support. The atlas exposes the conflict instead of selecting a silent consensus.
steps.annotation: Support values are conditional, not votes from nature.

steps.title: A branching polyp precedes the Cambrian
steps.text: Auroralumina supplies a crown-cnidarian hypothesis from a dated surface, while preserved anatomy and phylogenetic placement remain separate.
steps.annotation: One surface can test, not settle, a crown.

steps.title: A fibre-like impression is not histology
steps.text: Haootia shows ordered linear structures. Muscle and staurozoan readings remain explicit hypotheses with supporting and opposing studies.
steps.annotation: Visible pattern and tissue identity are different claims.

steps.title: More specimens can assemble a different animal
steps.text: Xianguangia joins fossils once named separately, but new anatomy also reopens whether the reconstructed body belongs on the cnidarian stem.
steps.annotation: Synonymy, anatomy and topology each need evidence.

steps.title: A bell and tentacles constrain a medusa
steps.text: Burgessomedusa supplies macroscopic medusa anatomy by the middle Cambrian. It is a bounded fossil sample, not the origin event itself.
steps.annotation: Minimum evidence is not a complete history.

steps.title: Some deep nodes resolve, one stays weak
steps.text: The sampled matrix supports Anthozoa and Medusozoa and several internal groups, but Ceriantharia keeps Hexacorallia uncertain.
steps.annotation: A supported subset is not a universal tree.

steps.title: Extreme reduction does not erase ancestry
steps.text: Myxozoan genomes place microscopic parasites inside Cnidaria. Their reduced bodies do not represent the ancestral cnidarian condition.
steps.annotation: Secondary loss must not be read as primitiveness.

steps.title: A clock can precede a skeleton
steps.text: Deep-water coral genes support an older split than the familiar Triassic skeleton record. Model time and fossil time stay separate.
steps.annotation: A posterior interval is not a hidden fossil.

steps.title: Skeleton chemistry records an ecological model
steps.text: Late-Triassic corals carry several proxy signals consistent with photosymbiosis. The symbiont is inferred, not fossilized.
steps.annotation: Proxy agreement strengthens but does not become direct observation.

title: Thirteen dossiers across molluscan and brachiopod body plans
titleZh: 横跨软体与腕足动物体制的十三个证据档案
dek: Move from named fossils to living genomes and experiments while keeping observation, homology, topology and nomenclature separate.

steps.title: A body outline remains mollusc-like, not crown-defined
steps.text: More than 35 White Sea specimens preserve bilateral organization and a dorsal cover, but no radula or crown-mollusc diagnosis.
steps.annotation: A named Ediacaran sample tests character homology without becoming a direct ancestor or global Mollusca first appearance.

steps.title: Repeated tooth rows make a radula testable
steps.text: Across 189 Odontogriphus specimens, paired teeth on a membrane show posterior replacement beside a broad foot and mantle groove.
steps.annotation: The geometry is observed; radular homology and stem-mollusc placement remain comparative conclusions.

steps.title: A shell and sclerites occur in one articulated body
steps.text: Orthrozanclus combines an anterior shell, three zones of imbricating sclerites and long marginal spines.
steps.annotation: Halwaxiida is a scored topology, not an observed ancestor chain or secure crown assignment.

steps.title: Shell sections separate laminae from nacre
steps.text: Pojetaia sections preserve a laminar inner fabric compared with foliated aragonite; undisputed Cambrian nacre is withheld.
steps.annotation: Preservation and homology limit mineral interpretation; the sections do not establish every bivalve shell pathway.

steps.title: A soft body tests a difficult cephalopod hypothesis
steps.text: Nectocaris has paired eyes, fins, two tentacles and a funnel-like structure in ninety newly prepared specimens.
steps.annotation: Missing shell, siphuncle, beak and radula evidence keeps the cephalopod placement explicitly contested.

steps.title: One phylogenomic matrix recovers Aculifera
steps.text: Chitons group with sampled aplacophorans, while gastropods and bivalves form another supported clade in the Kocot et al. analyses.
steps.annotation: Monoplacophora was absent and some alternatives were not rejected, so the result remains matrix-specific.

steps.title: A second matrix adds every major living group
steps.text: Fifteen new transcriptomes bring Monoplacophora into an all-class sample that recovers it with Cephalopoda in principal analyses.
steps.annotation: Conflicting deep nodes and corrected supplementary figures are retained rather than averaged into false certainty.

steps.title: Embryos connect Nodal to shell chirality
steps.text: Lottia and Biomphalaria express nodal and Pitx on opposite sides; inhibition disrupts pathway output and shell coiling.
steps.annotation: This living experiment does not directly reconstruct fossil torsion or every gastropod coiling mechanism.

steps.title: A genome tests cephalopod novelty without duplication
steps.text: One Octopus bimaculoides genome and twelve tissue transcriptomes reveal targeted family expansions and extensive rearrangement.
steps.annotation: Comparative association is not a single-gene cause of arms, suckers or neural complexity; whole-genome duplication was not supported.

steps.title: Two isolated sclerite types build a falsifiable model
steps.text: Micrina mitral and sellate sclerites have complementary geometry and muscle scars used to reconstruct a sessile bivalved animal.
steps.annotation: Articulation and valve homology are reconstructions, not a preserved whole organism or settled stem topology.

steps.title: A calcareous brachiopod preserves soft anatomy
steps.text: Kutorgina chengjiangensis preserves an early spirolophe, digestive tract and pedicle within paired valves.
steps.annotation: Direct anatomy informs comparison but does not make Kutorgina the ancestor of living rhynchonelliformeans.

steps.title: A living brachiopod shell is tested across three data layers
steps.text: The Lingula genome, staged transcriptomes and shell proteome separate shared components from lineage-specific phosphate-shell proteins.
steps.annotation: Shared genes do not imply shell identity, vertebrate bone homology or morphological stasis through the fossil record.

steps.title: A tube, valves and lophophore resist a simple ladder
steps.text: Yuganotheca combines paired agglutinated valves, a horseshoe lophophore, a bipartite tube and a long pedicle.
steps.annotation: COL26.8 routes 159,801 accepted living names here; that naming coverage cannot resolve this fossil mosaic or turn thirteen dossiers into an ancestor series.
